artists.biography:
"Little Simz"  (born Simbi Ajikawo), is a British rapper, singer and actress.  Simz studied at Highbury Fields School in London. She went on to attend St Mary’s Youth Club in Upper Street, Islington, where pop stars Leona Lewis and Alexandra Burke also attended. Simz later studied at Westminster Kingsway College and pursued her music career from there.
Acting--- After several months of auditioning by the BBC for the show Spirit Warriors, it was announced in June 2009 that Simz had been cast in the supporting role of Vicky.
In 2012, Simz joined the cast of E4's TV series Youngers as Meleka.
Music--- Simz often nicknamed "Bars Simzson" describes her music as rap and experimental and has performed alongside Estelle, Tinie Tempah and Ms. Dynamite.
The Award-winning North London born rapper + musician who has made her mark on a global scale with a series of critically acclaimed mixtapes and EPs, earning her global accolade as she soon became tipped to watch by the likes of VEVO, Red Bull, The Independent, BBC, The Guardian amongst many, landing her nominations for a bevy of awards including BET, MOBO and WORLDWIDE AWARDS (where she scooped up the Breakthrough Artist Of The Year trophy).

perplexity.description:
Project Unfollow is a hip-hop extended play released by Little Simz in 2018 on the Age 101 Music label. The project represents a continuation of the artist's independent output during the mid-to-late 2010s, arriving between her studio albums Stillness in Wonderland (2016) and Grey Area (2019). The EP features production and guest appearances, including contributions from collaborators like OTG and Tilla Arcé, with standout tracks including "Poison Ivy" and "Backseat."

Within Little Simz's broader discography, Project Unfollow occupies a transitional space in her artistic development. Released during a period when she was establishing herself as a distinctive voice in contemporary hip-hop, the project showcases her lyrical precision and introspective approach to the genre. The EP's relatively compact format allowed for focused artistic statements while maintaining the experimental spirit that characterized her earlier mixtapes and EPs.

While specific critical reception data is limited, Project Unfollow contributed to Little Simz's growing reputation as a serious hip-hop artist during this era. The project's vinyl release format reflects both the artist's commitment to physical media and the broader resurgence of vinyl collecting among hip-hop audiences in the late 2010s. By the time of its release, Little Simz had already established a dedicated fanbase through her independent releases and live performances at major festivals, positioning Project Unfollow as a significant entry in her catalog of self-directed work.
